encoding_notes: BOUNDARY TEST SCHEMA. This is the first theogonic (as opposed to emanationist) tradition in the corpus. The Derveni Papyrus preserves a 4th c. BCE commentary on an older Orphic theogonic poem. The cosmological sequence is reconstructed from cols. VIII-XXVI. Independence: HIGH -- the Derveni theogony predates all other traditions in the corpus by centuries (4th c. BCE vs. 2nd-3rd c. CE for the earliest emanation traditions). It is a pre-Socratic Greek cosmology with no derivation from Neoplatonism, Gnosticism, or Iranian religion. STRUCTURAL NOTE: Orphic cosmogony is theogonic (genealogical succession between divine rulers) rather than strictly emanationist (hierarchical overflow from a transcendent source). The DAG contract's edge-type vocabulary is extended with 'succession' for this schema -- defined as: the subsequent entity displaces or supersedes the prior entity in cosmological governance, typically through generational conflict. This distinction (emanation vs. succession) is well-documented in comparative religion scholarship (Bremmer 2008, West 1983). The key structural feature of the Derveni theogony is Zeus's swallowing: Zeus ingests the generative principle (aidoion) of the prior cosmos and re-emits all things from within himself. This is structurally closer to emanation-and-reabsorption than to simple genealogical succession. The Derveni commentator himself reads Zeus allegorically as Nous/Air -- an emanation interpretation already present in the 4th c. BCE.

nodes.name: Night (Nyx)
nodes.description: The primordial principle in the Derveni theogony. Night is the first to prophesy and the first to rule (col. X). She is not generated from any prior entity -- she is the self-existent origin of the theogonic sequence. Night's prophetic function is structurally significant: she gives oracles to Zeus (col. XI), providing the knowledge by which he reconstitutes the cosmos. In some readings, Night is prior to the cosmic egg; in the Derveni sequence, she is the apex.
nodes.source_reference: Derveni Papyrus col. X (Kouremenos et al. 2006)

nodes.name: Ouranos (Sky)
nodes.description: Born from Night; the first king of the gods in the Derveni succession. Ouranos rules the cosmos as its first sovereign. He is called 'first-born' (protogonos in some reconstructions, though this is debated). His kingship ends when Kronos displaces him through castration -- the severed generative organ (aidoion) becomes a key cosmological object in the Derveni narrative. The edge from Night to Ouranos is typed 'emanation' rather than 'succession' because Ouranos does not displace Night -- he is generated from her and rules alongside/after her prophetic establishment of order.
nodes.source_reference: Derveni Papyrus cols. XIII-XIV (Kouremenos et al. 2006)

nodes.name: Kronos (Time)
nodes.description: Seizes kingship from Ouranos through castration -- the defining act of the theogonic succession. Kronos' rule represents the second age of the cosmos. The Derveni commentator interprets the castration allegorically (col. XIII): the separation of generative power from the prior cosmic order. This act of violent displacement is the paradigmatic 'succession' event in Orphic theogony -- structurally distinct from emanation (which is non-violent, non-diminishing overflow). Kronos is in turn overthrown by Zeus.
nodes.source_reference: Derveni Papyrus col. XIII (Kouremenos et al. 2006)

nodes.name: Zeus (The Reconstituter)
nodes.description: Overthrows Kronos; receives oracles from Night (col. XI); and performs the critical cosmological act: he swallows the aidoion (generative organ of Ouranos/the prior cosmos) and thereby contains ALL prior beings within himself. He then re-emits (re-generates) the entire cosmos from within. The Derveni commentator reads Zeus as Nous or Air (col. XVI-XVII) -- a cosmic intelligence that reconstitutes reality through ingestion and re-emanation. This swallowing-and-reconstitution is structurally closer to the RHC fold operation (F = i/2) than to simple genealogical succession: Zeus absorbs the prior cosmic order and outputs a reconstituted one. He is both the successor-king and the demiurgic re-creator. This dual role (succession + creation) makes Zeus the structural pivot of the Derveni schema.
nodes.source_reference: Derveni Papyrus cols. XV-XIX (Kouremenos et al. 2006); Betegh 2004 ch. 5-7

nodes.name: Reconstituted Cosmos (Zeus's Re-Emission)
nodes.description: The cosmos as reconstituted by Zeus after swallowing and re-emitting all prior beings. The Derveni commentator describes Zeus re-emitting heaven, sea, earth, rivers, and the gods themselves (col. XVII-XIX). This is NOT creation from nothing but RE-creation from absorbed substance -- Zeus outputs a reconstituted cosmos that contains all prior beings in new form. The material world is the product of divine reconstitution, not of fall or corruption. This is the terminal node: the physical cosmos as organized by Zeus/Nous.
nodes.source_reference: Derveni Papyrus cols. XVII-XIX (Kouremenos et al. 2006)

edges.description: Night generates Ouranos as the first cosmic ruler. This is typed 'emanation' rather than 'succession' because Ouranos does not displace Night -- he emerges from her and receives her prophetic oracles. Night remains the oracular authority even after Ouranos rules.

Kronos displaces Ouranos through castration, seizing kingship. This is the paradigmatic succession event: the later entity overthrows and replaces the earlier. 'Succession' is defined as: the subsequent entity displaces or supersedes the prior entity in cosmological governance, typically through generational conflict. This edge type is unique to the Derveni schema and represents a genuine structural difference from emanation (non-diminishing overflow) and creation (deliberate fabrication).
Zeus overthrows Kronos, seizing kingship. Second succession event. Zeus then performs the cosmological swallowing that distinguishes the Derveni theogony from simple genealogical succession.

Zeus re-emits the cosmos from within himself after swallowing the aidoion and all prior beings. This is typed 'creation' rather than 'emanation' because it is a deliberate, singular act of cosmic reconstitution. The Derveni commentator interprets it as Nous/Air organizing all matter (col. XVI-XVII). Structurally comparable to the demiurgic creation edge in other schemas.

rhapsodic_expanded.description: Expanded encoding using the Orphic Rhapsodies (Bernabe 2004) instead of the Derveni Papyrus. Adds Chronos (Unaging Time) at the apex, Cosmic Egg, Phanes/Protogonos, and Dionysus/Zagreus + Humanity at the bottom. 8-10 nodes, depth 7-8.
rhapsodic_expanded.scholarly_support: The Rhapsodies provide a longer, more elaborate theogonic sequence. However, the Rhapsodies are reconstructed from late-antique quotations (Damascius, Proclus, Athenagoras) rather than a single physical text. Textual stability is lower than the Derveni Papyrus.

nodes_added.name: Chronos (Unaging Time)
nodes_added.description: The Rhapsodic first principle. Co-present with Ananke (Necessity) and Aither.

nodes_added.name: Cosmic Egg
nodes_added.description: Generated by Chronos/Ananke coiling around proto-matter.

nodes_added.name: Phanes/Protogonos (First-Born)
nodes_added.description: Hatches from the Egg; golden-winged, bisexual, radiant first god. Functions exactly like a Neoplatonic first emanation.

nodes_added.name: Dionysus/Zagreus
nodes_added.description: Son of Zeus and Persephone; receives sceptre; dismembered by Titans.

nodes_added.name: Humanity (from Titan Ashes)
nodes_added.description: Arises from Titan ashes mixed with Dionysian divinity.

rhapsodic_expanded.encoding_note: DEFERRED TO WP 1.4. The Rhapsodies are too reconstructive for a methodology paper that needs to convince DH reviewers of encoding rigour. The Derveni Papyrus is a single physical text with a defensible reconstruction.

all_emanation_edges.description: Alternative encoding mapping all edges to 'emanation' without the 'succession' edge type. Treats theogonic succession as a variant of emanation (the later entity proceeds from the earlier). This preserves compatibility with the WP 1.1 edge-type vocabulary at the cost of obscuring the structural difference between overflow and displacement.
all_emanation_edges.scholarly_support: The Derveni commentator's own allegorical reading (Zeus = Nous/Air) supports treating the theogonic sequence as emanation in disguise. However, this reading is the commentator's philosophical overlay on the original poem, not the poem's own structure.
all_emanation_edges.encoding_note: LOW priority sensitivity alternative. Tests whether edge-type distinction affects topology-family classification. Under GED computation, edge labels are typically not weighted, so this may not change quantitative results.
